look_here_first: LOOK HERE FIRST: Follow the glossy black stipe into the black rachis all the way through the narrow once-pinnate blade. Check the many small oblong pinnae, usually with a tiny upper-side basal ear (acroscopic auricle). Turn a fertile pinna over to look for 2–5 pairs of elongated sori.

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Small perennial fern rooted in shaded rock cracks and limestone or other basic rock; fronds narrow, commonly 9–20 cm long.

key_traits.label: Leaves attachment
key_traits.text: Frond once pinnate throughout, with roughly 20–40 pairs of oblong pinnae; margins entire to shallowly scalloped; small acroscopic auricle often present at pinna base.

key_traits.label: Flower reproductive
key_traits.text: Ferns lack flowers. Mature pinnae bear usually 2–5 pairs of elongate sori along veins on the underside; a thin indusium covers young sori.

key_traits.label: Fruit seed
key_traits.text: No fruit or seeds; spores develop in sporangia inside the underside sori.

key_traits.label: Stem bud
key_traits.text: Petiole (stipe) and leaf axis (rachis) are glossy black throughout, unlike relatives with green upper rachises.
